newsitem.title: CHILE: Endesa says to prepay World Bank loans.
newsitem.headline: Endesa says to prepay World Bank loans.

text.p: Chilean power giant Endesa said its Pangue unit will prepay loans totalling $150 million to the World Bank's financial wing International Finance Corp (IFC).
"The decision...was adopted after analyzing different offers from international banks which offered better terms than the loan granted by the IFC," said the statement.

The move follows a public spat between the company and bank officials over alleged breaches of environmental obligations at Endesa's controversial Pangue and Ralco dam projects on the southern Bio Bio river.
In a letter addressed to Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, Bank president James Wolfensohn threated last month to declare Endesa in default of its commitments under the terms of the loans.
Endesa said it will prepay the loans using a a new five-year credit from the Dresdner Bank with an interest rate of Libor plus 0.25 percent, which is lower than the rate for the IFC loan.
"The decision has a clear advantage for all the shareholders in Pangue, including the IFC itself, which owns 2.5 percent of the company," said the statement.
Pangue came on stream last year and building work has recently started on the much larger Ralco hydro-electric plant.
The Ralco project has raised the hackles of ecologists as it will flood a large area of the wooded Bio Bio valley and force hundreds of Pehuenche Indians from their homes.
